{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-id-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"322fcb13cd93c68e77afa7dde2fe9075c301171e825e65259ca1dbe52c9cc780","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-id-class-d:lineage:23","source_registry_sha256":"9c432577e712960022ff656d6738a091319c6e5e4dcbdcf9429cd450e142e543","source_liveness_sha256":"eee60602368bd429216c9c2833be0be6ed9e505e5c5accebaefb9d2b9a847475"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Traffic signs and work zones","heading":"C — Traffic signs and work zones","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Traffic signs and work zones

FACT_ID: sec05-F01 | anchor: A44
Traffic signals, signs and pavement markings are traffic-control devices. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F02 | anchor: A44
Drivers must obey traffic directions given by law enforcement officers, highway personnel and school crossing guards. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F03 | anchor: A44
Learn to recognize traffic signs by their color, shape and written message or symbol. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F04 | anchor: A44
Regulatory signs are usually black and white, although some use red and white. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F05 | anchor: A44
At a stop sign, stop at the clearly marked stop line when one is present. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F06 | anchor: A44
At a stop sign without a stop line, stop before the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F07 | anchor: A44
At a stop sign with neither a stop line nor a crosswalk, stop before entering the intersecting highway at the nearest point where approaching traffic can be seen. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F08 | anchor: A44
A Yield sign requires slowing and yielding to vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection being crossed or on the road being entered. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F09 | anchor: A44
At a Yield sign, stop before crossing the intersection or entering the highway if that is necessary to yield safely. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec05-F10 | anchor: A45
A Do Not Enter sign prohibits entry to that highway section from the direction being traveled. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F11 | anchor: A45
A speed-limit sign states the maximum speed for that road section under ideal driving conditions. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F12 | anchor: A45
A Keep Right of Island sign directs traffic to the right of the island or barrier ahead. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec05-F13 | anchor: A46
Work zones commonly use orange signs, cones, drums, barricades or flashing arrow panels to identify the area. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-F14 | anchor: A46
In a work zone, watch for hazards such as uneven pavement, narrow lanes, heavy equipment and gravel. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-F15 | anchor: A46
Work-zone warning signs use orange and black. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-F16 | anchor: A46
Do not move or go around barriers or signs to cross onto a road closed to traffic. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-F17 | anchor: A46
When a lane-shift sign redirects all lanes, remain in the same lane while following its shift. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec05-F18 | anchor: A47
A Be Prepared to Stop sign calls for slowing and readiness to stop for road work ahead. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F19 | anchor: A47
A slow-moving-vehicle warning calls for reducing speed and approaching the vehicle cautiously. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F20 | anchor: A47
The handbook says the slow-moving-vehicle sign is used mainly on off-road equipment such as farm and construction vehicles. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F21 | anchor: A47
A Road Closed sign prohibits entry to the work zone except by authorized personnel. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F22 | anchor: A47
A closure marked Local Traffic Only or Closed to Thru Traffic permits local residential or commercial traffic only when it has a reason to stop within the work zone. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F23 | anchor: A47
Properly posted work-zone closure signs prohibit continuous trips through the closed work zone. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec05-F24 | anchor: A48
Work-zone speeding fines are increased where signs indicate the increase. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-F25 | anchor: A48
Watch closely for work-zone personnel because they may work near traffic during both daytime and nighttime. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-F26 | anchor: A48
Leave ample space behind the vehicle ahead while traveling through a work zone. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-F27 | anchor: A48
In work zones, allow extra time and reduce distractions such as phones and the stereo. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-F28 | anchor: A48
Speeding, inattention, failure to yield and improper lane changes contribute to work-zone crashes. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-F29 | anchor: A48
Motorists must follow directions from a school safety patrol official. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-F30 | anchor: A48
School-appointed safety patrol officials identify their duty through a badge, appropriate clothing or School Patrol insignia. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-F31 | anchor: A48
School safety patrol officials display stop or other directional signs where schoolchildren cross public roads. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec05-F32 | anchor: A49
Most warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-F33 | anchor: A49
School warning signs may use fluorescent yellow-green. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-F34 | anchor: A49
A warning sign indicates an unexpected condition that may require slowing or another response. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-F35 | anchor: A49
An Open Range sign identifies an area where livestock may roam unfenced and have the right of way. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-F36 | anchor: A49
The handbook's T-intersection warning describes a junction where the driver must turn left or right. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-F37 | anchor: A49
At the T-intersection described by the handbook's warning, stop and yield to drivers approaching from either crossing direction. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-F38 | anchor: A49
An intersection or crossroads warning calls for watching for cross-traffic from the road crossing ahead. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec05-F39 | anchor: A49
A Traffic Signal Ahead sign warns of an upcoming signalized intersection and is used on roads with higher speeds or blocked views of the intersection or signal. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-id-d:idaho-transportation-department-division:handbook:pdf-0049]

Misconceptions: A local-traffic closure allows a reason to stop inside the zone, rather than uninterrupted travel through it.
Mnemonic: Read, slow and follow is a teaching reminder for device messages and directed travel.
Glossary: Regulatory signs state control; warning signs identify unexpected conditions; guide signs provide direction or destination information.
Dynamic facts: local closures, posted penalty notices and crossing-specific contact details are not frozen into invented values.
